title: Heated Throws for Parents and Grandparents: What They Cost and How to Use One Safely
subtitle: A plug-in heated throw can take the chill off an evening in the armchair, as long as you pick one with auto shut-off and use it with care.
excerpt: A heated throw warms the person, not the whole house. Here is how auto shut-off works, what to check before buying one as a gift, and the habits that help keep it safe.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: If someone you love is always chilly in the recliner, it is natural to look for a way to keep them comfortable without heating the whole house. A heated throw is one option people consider.

A plug-in heated throw is a lap-sized blanket that warms the person sitting under it. It can make a thoughtful gift for a parent or grandparent, provided you choose carefully and set a few ground rules.
The throw plugs into a wall outlet. A small controller on a cord lets you turn it on and pick a heat level. The Serta throws below use soft, flexible wires and offer 5 heat settings.

The most important feature is auto shut-off, meaning the throw turns itself off after a set time. According to NBC News Select, this is typically 3 to 4 hours or set by the user. Experts there also warn that a heated blanket can cause a fire if used improperly, so auto shut-off is a help, not a substitute for care.

Be clear about what a throw cannot do. It warms one spot, so it does not replace home heating. It needs a nearby outlet, and the cord can become a trip hazard. Both Serta throws shut off after 3 hours, so they switch off partway through a long evening, and some people find restarting them fiddly.
Who should check with a doctor first

Electric bedding is not advised for infants, people who cannot move easily on their own, or anyone who has trouble sensing heat, such as someone with poor circulation. If your parent has neuropathy (nerve damage that dulls feeling) or diabetes, ask their doctor before buying one.

"An over-heating condition may not be obvious to the user, but can result in a thermal burn if exposed long enough." — Joel Hawk, Principal Engineer for electric bedding at Underwriters Laboratories, quoted by TODAY.com

items: Auto shut-off: treat it as essential, and note how long the timer runs.
Overheating protection: check that the product page lists it.

Independent safety approval: the Serta pages list ETL certification. TODAY.com, in an older article, suggests looking for independent lab approval such as UL. The Medical King page does not state any safety certification, so ask before buying.
A controller that suits the hands using it: stiff fingers and small buttons do not mix, so look at the controller before gifting.
Cord length: both Serta throws have a 72-inch power cord and a 36-inch controller cord. A long cord can be a trip hazard, so plan where it will run.
Washing instructions: the Serta throws are machine washable. Unplug the throw and detach the controller first, and dry it fully before reuse.
The real price: list prices run high and store sale prices shift with coupons, so compare before you buy. The Serta throws listed here have no monthly fee.

sections.content: For a rough comparison, NBC News Select listed electric blankets, which are a different product from these throws, at about $36 to $50 in September 2026: Tefici and Bedsure on Amazon, and Brookstone at Target. We have not checked how they compare with the throws above.
Setting it up and using it safely
Pick a chair close to an outlet and run the cord where nobody will trip on it, not across a walkway.

Show your parent how the controller works, and walk through the buttons together. Never leave a heated throw on unattended, and turn it off when you go to sleep. Follow the maker's instructions about using it with other bedding.

To wash it, unplug it and detach the controller first, then let it dry completely before using it again. Heated throws have a limited lifespan, so check it now and then. If it looks frayed, kinked or scorched, retire it and replace it.
Check for open recalls on any model before you buy, and never buy a heated throw secondhand. Check the controller before gifting, since buttons and cords can be fiddly for stiff hands.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: Used sensibly, a heated throw can be a cozy way to help someone you love stay comfortable through the winter. Set it up together, and it may become the favorite spot in the house.
